title: 14/15 scenarios passed; scene_object_fixture fails on robot-only output
summary: The CI run tested 15 scenarios covering builtin, cap, and flow families. 14 passed; the single failure is `scene_object_fixture`, which calls `robonix/system/scene/list_objects` and expects at least one non-robot object (label != "robot") in the output. The scene service returned only the robot self-object (`scene.object.robot_001`) across all 45 rounds, causing the regex assertion `"label":\s*"(?!robot)[^"]+"` to fail. All other scenarios (camera/lidar snapshots, explore, navigation, memory, speech, voiceprint, mapping, fault recovery, patrol observe, object navigation) passed successfully.

test_result: Webots CI exercised 15 scenarios: 4 builtin (fault_recovery_builtin, file_roundtrip, plan_control_builtins, run_command), 7 cap (camera_snapshot, explore_smoke, lidar_snapshot, mapping_save, memory_roundtrip, scene_object_fixture, speech_speak, voiceprint_list), and 3 flow (fault_recovery, object_navigation, patrol_observe). 14 passed. The failing scenario `scene_object_fixture` called `list_objects` 45 times; each time the scene service returned only the robot self-object, so the test's regex assertion for a non-robot label failed.
likely_root_cause: The scene service's perception pipeline (concept-graphs detector) did not detect any non-robot objects during the test window. The registry contained only the robot self-object (`scene.object.robot_001`). This is likely because the Webots simulation world used in CI has no furniture or objects placed in the robot's field of view, or the perception models (YOLO-World, MobileSAM) did not fire within the test duration.

evidence.text: All 45 rounds return only robot_001 with label "robot".
failed — persistence OFF for this session (no restore, no writes): No module named 'pymilvus'

suggested_fix: Ensure the Webots CI world includes at least one non-robot object (e.g., a table, chair, or box) within the robot's initial field of view so the perception pipeline has something to detect. Alternatively, adjust the test to accept a robot-only scene as valid (e.g., relax the regex or add a separate test for empty scenes). The pymilvus import error is a pre-existing environment issue and does not affect this test.
risks_or_watchouts: The scene_object_fixture test will continue to fail in CI unless the simulation world is populated with objects.
The pymilvus import error prevents object memory persistence, but does not affect the current test failure.
Other scenarios (explore, navigation) rely on the robot being able to move and detect objects; they passed, indicating the robot can navigate but no objects were detected.
